voices.note: the baraita's first tanna: monetary cases by three

props.gloss_en: monetary cases are judged by three
monetary cases are judged by five
(entertained) the written 'three' refers to the verdict stage, so five must sit that three conclude the verdict
(inside the hypothesis) the great Sanhedrin would need 141 so that the verdict is concluded by 71
(inside the hypothesis) the small Sanhedrin would need 45 so that the verdict is concluded by 23
the counts are anchored at the start: seventy from the moment of gathering, and likewise three from the moment of the litigant's approach -- not at the verdict stage
yarshi'un is read as a plural: the verse's lower mention speaks of two judges
yarshi'un is written defectively -- the Rabbanan follow the consonantal text, which is singular
a court may not be evenly balanced -- one judge is added to the four

schemas.gloss_en: Elohim below (yarshi'un = two) and Elohim above: as below two, so above two; a court may not be even -- add one: five judges
